title: Clafoutis
subtitle: French baked cherry custard pudding
excerpt: A classic Limousin dessert: fresh cherries baked in a batter that is somewhere between a thick custard and a thin pancake, puffed at the edges and set at the centre, dusted with icing sugar. Simple, seasonal, and better warm from the oven than anything more elaborate.

recipe.sourceNotes: Clafoutis comes from the Limousin region of central France and takes its name from the Occitan word clafir, meaning to fill. It is traditionally made with whole cherries left unpitted, which is not carelessness but intention: the cherry stones release a subtle almond-like flavour during baking that improves the finished dish. The batter is a simple mixture of eggs, flour, milk, cream, and sugar, similar to a crêpe batter but slightly thicker. It is poured over cherries arranged in a buttered gratin dish and baked until puffed and golden. Variations using other fruits are sometimes called flaugnarde rather than clafoutis, though the distinction is informal. Serve warm rather than hot, with a dusting of icing sugar.

content.text: The batter should be the consistency of double cream: smooth and just pourable. Leave the cherry stones in if you are using fresh cherries; the flavour is worth the inconvenience. Do not overbake: the centre should tremble slightly when the dish is moved and will set completely as it cools. A perfectly baked clafoutis is creamy inside; an overbaked one is rubbery.

items.preparation: use fresh cherries if available; or mixed stone fruit; stalks removed but stones left in if using cherries

content.text: Heat the oven to 180°C / fan 160°C / gas 4. Butter a 30 cm shallow gratin dish generously and dust with 2 tablespoons of sugar, tipping out the excess. Arrange the cherries (or other fruit) in a single layer.
Whisk the eggs and 80 g sugar until combined. Whisk in the flour until smooth, then gradually whisk in the milk and cream to form a smooth, pourable batter. Add the vanilla.

Pour the batter over the fruit. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the edges are puffed and golden and the centre is just set with a slight tremor. Leave to cool for 10 minutes. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm from the dish.
